subproblems.title: Null transfer to slices: Hⁿ-a.e. properties on M hold H^m-a.e. on almost every slice M ∩ f⁻¹{t}
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be arbitrary, and write Hᵏ := μHE[k]. Assume the co-area identity for (M, f, G): for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], the function t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m (lower Lebesgue integral of g for H^m restricted to M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) is L¹-a.e.-measurable on ℝ and ∫_ℝ (∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m) dt = ∫_M |G| g dH^{m+1}. Then for every predicate p on ℝ^P that holds for H^{m+1}-a.e. x ∈ M (∀ᵐ x ∂(H^{m+1} restricted to M), p x), for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ the predicate p holds for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} (∀ᵐ x ∂(H^m restricted to M ∩ f⁻¹{t}), p x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (G : Eucl P → Eucl P), (∀ g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → AEMeasurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P))) (volume : Measure ℝ) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P))) ∂(volume : Measure ℝ) = ∫⁻ x in M, ‖G x‖ₑ * g x ∂(μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P))) → ∀ p : Eucl P → Prop, (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), p x) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t})), p x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k). Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P). L¹ := volume on ℝ. For a measure μ and a set S, μ⌞S := μ.restrict S. (CA) denotes the co-area hypothesis of the statement: for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_M |G|ₑ g dH^{m+1}. It is verbatim the conclusion of slicing_im_coarea, the sibling on which the parent node slicing_im_slice_triple depends; it enters here as a hypothesis because children may depend only on their own siblings.
This is Step 1 (null transfer, NT) of the parent proof (slicing_im_slice_triple), stated for an arbitrary predicate.
1. (Measurable null hull.) Let N := {x ∈ ℝ^P : ¬p(x)}. The hypothesis ∀ᵐ x ∂(H^{m+1}⌞M), p x says (H^{m+1}⌞M)(N) = 0 (ae_iff). Let Z := toMeasurable (H^{m+1}⌞M) N. Then Z is a measurable set, N ⊆ Z (subset_toMeasurable) and (H^{m+1}⌞M)(Z) = (H^{m+1}⌞M)(N) = 0 (measure_toMeasurable).
2. (Co-area with an indicator.) The indicator g := 1_Z = Z.indicator 1 : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] is measurable (Z is measurable). By (CA), F(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} 1_Z dH^m is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ F(t) dt = ∫_M |G(x)|ₑ·1_Z(x) dH^{m+1}(x).
3. (The right side vanishes.) The integrand x ↦ |G(x)|ₑ·1_Z(x) is 0 at every x ∉ Z. Since (H^{m+1}⌞M)(Z) = 0, it vanishes (H^{m+1}⌞M)-a.e., so its integral with respect to H^{m+1}⌞M is 0 (lintegral_congr_ae, lintegral_zero). Hence ∫_ℝ F(t) dt = 0.
4. (F = 0 a.e.) F is a.e.-measurable, nonnegative, and has integral 0, so F(t) = 0 for L¹-a.e. t (lintegral_eq_zero_iff').
5. (Conclusion.) Fix t with F(t) = 0. As Z is measurable, F(t) = ∫ 1_Z d(H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})) = (H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}))(Z) (lintegral_indicator_one). By monotonicity (N ⊆ Z), (H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}))(N) ≤ (H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}))(Z) = 0, i.e. ∀ᵐ x ∂(H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})), p x (ae_iff). This holds for L¹-a.e. t, which is the claim. ∎
(No measurability of M, f, G and no bound on G is used. Downstream, p then also holds H^m-a.e. on every subset of M ∩ f⁻¹{t}, in particular on M_t (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), and countably many such conclusions combine by ae_all_iff.)
proof_key_steps: Replace the exceptional set N = {¬p} by its measurable hull Z for H^{m+1}⌞M, which is still null.
Apply the co-area hypothesis to g = 1_Z: ∫_ℝ (H^m⌞(M∩f⁻¹{t}))(Z) dt = ∫_M |G|·1_Z dH^{m+1} = 0.
An a.e.-measurable nonnegative function with zero integral vanishes a.e., so (H^m⌞(M∩f⁻¹{t}))(Z) = 0 for a.e. t.
Monotonicity N ⊆ Z gives ∀ᵐ x ∂H^m⌞(M∩f⁻¹{t}), p x for a.e. t.

subproblems.title: Null-measurability of M_t, local integrability of θ on M_t and a.e. strong measurability of ξ_t for a.e. t

Write Hᵏ := μHE[k] and assume the co-area identity for (M, f, G): for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_M |G| g dHⁿ. For t ∈ ℝ let M_t := {x ∈ M : f(x) = t, G(x) ≠ 0} and ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ∘ ι(|G(x)|⁻¹G(x)), where ι(v) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ ℝ^P ℝ) ∘ (smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m (innerSL ℝ v)) : Λ^m → Λ^{m+1} (ι(v)α = v♭∧α). Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ: (a) M_t is H^m-null-measurable; (b) θ is H^m-integrable on M_t ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U; (c) ξ_t is a.e. strongly measurable for H^m restricted to M_t.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P; on ℝᵏ it equals Lebesgue measure Lᵏ = volume, and H⁰ is counting measure). L¹ := volume on ℝ. For a measure μ and a set S, μ⌞S := μ.restrict S, and 'p holds μ-a.e. on S' means ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ⌞S), p x. n := m + 1. M_t := {x ∈ M : f(x) = t, G(x) ≠ 0}. For v ∈ ℝ^P, ι(v) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ ℝ^P ℝ) ∘L (smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m (innerSL ℝ v)) : Λ^m → Λ^{m+1}; by `rfl` ι(v)α = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α) =: v♭∧α, and by `alternatizeUncurryFin_apply` (v♭∧α)(v₀,…,v_m) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i ⟨v, v_i⟩ α(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_m). ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ∘L ι(|G(x)|⁻¹G(x)). (CA) denotes the co-area hypothesis for (M, f, G): for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_M |G|ₑ g dHⁿ; it is verbatim the conclusion of slicing_im_coarea, the sibling on which the parent node slicing_im_slice_triple depends, and enters here as a hypothesis because children may depend only on their own siblings. TG(f, G) denotes the tangential-gradient property: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every subspace Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q, G(x) ∈ Q and s ↦ f(x + su) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0 for every u ∈ Q.
This is Steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 of the parent proof (slicing_im_slice_triple).
0. (Null transfer.) The sibling ae_transfer (slicing_im_st_ae_transfer), applied to (P, m, M, f, G) and (CA), gives (NT): if a predicate p holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., then for L¹-a.e. t it holds H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e., hence also H^m⌞S-a.e. for every S ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), in particular for S = M_t and S = M_t ∩ K. Countably many statements 'for L¹-a.e. t' combine (ae_all_iff).
1. (Exhaustion of U.) Let (B̄_k)_{k∈ℕ} enumerate the closed balls closedBall(q, ρ) with q ∈ ℚ^P, ρ ∈ ℚ, ρ > 0 and closedBall(q, ρ) ⊆ U (if there are none, U = ∅ and all K_i := ∅), and put K_i := ⋃_{k≤i} B̄_k. Each K_i is compact and K_i ⊆ U. Every x ∈ U lies in the open ball ball(q_k, ρ_k) of some B̄_k: choose r > 0 with ball(x, 2r) ⊆ U, then q rational with |q − x| < r/2 and ρ rational in (r/2, r). Hence every compact K ⊆ U is covered by finitely many of these open balls, so K ⊆ K_N for the largest index N used, and ⋃_i K_i = U. (Do not use K_i := {x : |x| ≤ i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/i}: in Lean, infDist to the empty set is 0, so for U = ℝ^P these sets would be empty.)
2. (Borel modifications.) By the field integrableOn, θ is Hⁿ-integrable, hence Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K_i)-a.e. strongly measurable, for every i. Since M ⊆ U = ⋃_i K_i, M = ⋃_i (M ∩ K_i), so θ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff). Choose a strongly measurable θ̃ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ̃ ≥ 0 and θ = θ̃ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.: take the AEStronglyMeasurable.mk version θ₀ of θ (ae_eq_mk) and θ̃ := max(θ₀, 0), which is still strongly measurable and equals θ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. because θ > 0 on M (field pos). Also, by the field aestronglyMeasurable, a strongly measurable ξ̃ : ℝ^P → Λ_n with ξ = ξ̃ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. By the field nullMeasurableSet choose a measurable B ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0 (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). Then the predicate p₁(x) :⟺ (x ∈ B ∧ θ(x) = θ̃(x) ∧ ξ(x) = ξ̃(x)) holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.; for the first conjunct, (Hⁿ⌞M){x ∉ B} = Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply₀').
3. (Transfer.) By (NT), for L¹-a.e. t, p₁ holds H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e.
4. (Finite slice integrals of θ̃.) Fix i. The function g_i := 1_{K_i}·ofReal∘θ̃ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] is measurable. By (CA), J_i(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g_i dH^m is L¹-a.e.-measurable in t and
   ∫_ℝ J_i(t) dt = ∫_M |G|ₑ g_i dHⁿ ≤ L·∫_{M∩K_i} ofReal(θ̃) dHⁿ = L·∫_{M∩K_i} ofReal(θ) dHⁿ ≤ L·∫_{M∩K_i} |θ|ₑ dHⁿ < ∞,
   using |G| ≤ L, θ = θ̃ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., and the integrability of θ on M ∩ K_i (field integrableOn with K := K_i). Hence J_i(t) < ∞ for L¹-a.e. t (ae_lt_top'). As K_i is measurable, J_i(t) = ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}∩K_i} ofReal(θ̃) dH^m (lintegral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict). By ae_all_iff, for L¹-a.e. t, J_i(t) < ∞ for all i simultaneously.
5. Fix t in the intersection of the full-measure sets of steps 3 and 4. We prove (a)–(c) for this t.
   (a) (nullMeasurableSet; parent Step 5.) M_t = (B ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ G⁻¹(ℝ^P ∖ {0})) ∪ ((M ∖ B) ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ G⁻¹(ℝ^P ∖ {0})). The first set is measurable (B measurable, f and G measurable). The second set is contained in Y := Bᶜ ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{t}), and H^m(Y) ≤ (H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}))(Bᶜ) = 0 by step 3 (Measure.le_restrict_apply). A union of a measurable set and an H^m-null set is H^m-null-measurable (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet, NullMeasurableSet.of_null, NullMeasurableSet.union). So M_t is H^m-null-measurable.
   (b) (integrableOn; parent Step 4.) Let K ⊆ U be compact and choose i with K ⊆ K_i (step 1). Since M_t ∩ K_i ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}, step 3 gives θ = θ̃ H^m⌞(M_t ∩ K_i)-a.e.; θ̃ being strongly measurable, θ is H^m⌞(M_t ∩ K_i)-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr).    ∫_{M_t∩K_i} |θ|ₑ dH^m = ∫_{M_t∩K_i} ofReal(θ̃) dH^m ≤ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}∩K_i} ofReal(θ̃) dH^m = J_i(t) < ∞
   (lintegral_mono_set, using M_t ∩ K_i ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K_i). Thus θ is H^m-integrable on M_t ∩ K_i, hence on the subset M_t ∩ K (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
   (c) (aestronglyMeasurable; parent Step 6.) First, v ↦ ι(v) ∈ (Λ^m →L Λ^{m+1}) is continuous. Do not argue this by viewing smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m as a continuous map: at this Mathlib pin instance search fails on its codomain Λ^m →L (ℝ^P →L Λ^m). Instead: by rfl and alternatizeUncurryFin_apply, (ι(v)α)(σ) = Σ_i (−1)^i ⟨v, σ_i⟩ α(removeNth i σ). Hence ι(v) − ι(w) = ι(v − w) (ext; inner_sub_left, sub_mul, smul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib), and ‖ι(u)‖ ≤ (m+1)|u| (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound together with ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_alternatizeUncurryFin_le, ContinuousLinearMap.norm_smulRight_apply and innerSL_apply_norm). So ι is (m+1)-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul), hence continuous. The map ν(x) := |G(x)|⁻¹G(x) is measurable (G measurable; Measurable.norm, Measurable.inv, Measurable.smul), hence strongly measurable into ℝ^P, and x ↦ ι(ν(x)) is strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable). Composition (A, B) ↦ A ∘L B, from (Λ^{m+1} →L ℝ) × (Λ^m →L Λ^{m+1}) to Λ^m →L ℝ, is continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_comp.continuous). So ξ̃_t(x) := ξ̃(x) ∘L ι(ν(x)) is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.prodMk, then Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable). This route has been compiled at this pin. By step 3 and M_t ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}, ξ = ξ̃ holds H^m⌞M_t-a.e., and at every such x, ξ_t(x) = ξ̃_t(x). Hence ξ_t = ξ̃_t H^m⌞M_t-a.e. and ξ_t is H^m⌞M_t-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr).
6. (a)–(c) hold for every t in a set of full L¹-measure, which proves the claim. ∎

subproblems.title: Weighted approximate tangent planes on a C¹ antilipschitz chart (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.8(1))
subproblems.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^Q open, M ⊆ V Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q), and θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ with θ > 0 on M and θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V. Let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q of class C¹, and c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M ∩ Φ(Ω) and every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = y, the subspace DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) (LinearMap.range of fderiv ℝ Φ w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at y in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y).

Provenance and role. This is the 'tangent identification' fact isolated in Steps 7 and 9 of the parent proof (slicing_im_slice_triple: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.8(1), weighted version). In this split it is used twice, with V := U: in dimension m+1 for (M, θ) on the charts Φ_j (sibling chart_data, step 5) and in dimension m for (M_t, θ) on the level-set charts Ψ_{j,i} (sibling slice_geometry, step 6). Its frozen Lean type is byte-identical to that of lpf_weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart (DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart-a1), which is not yet comparator-accepted and therefore cannot be reused by name here. The proof below is that node's independently reviewed natural proof, which follows Simon's printed arguments (proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.8(1), specialized to one C¹ chart); it is self-contained. Other DAG declarations, such as the comparator-accepted lpf_wtc_* lemmas that prove pieces of steps 0–4, may be used only after they are added as reuse children (byte-identical type and lean_name) at a decomposition of this node. The parent's parenthetical sketch uses Lebesgue points of θ. Simon's printed Remark 1.8(1), followed here, instead uses Lusin pieces on which θ is continuous; both give the same three error terms.

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. Hⁿ = μHE[n], Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure. On ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume; it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx; and H⁰ is counting measure. A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w.

This lemma is Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4/1.7, the proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.8(1), specialized to one C¹ chart. Setting: V ⊆ ℝ^Q open, M ⊆ V Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V; Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q of class C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ c-antilipschitz on Ω (c > 0). Put N := Φ(Ω). Recall η_{y,λ}(z) := λ⁻¹(z − y) (`blowUpMap y λ`) and that HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P means: dim P = n and for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_P φ dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0. If n > Q then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^Q (Hausdorff dimension of ℝ^Q is Q; `hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt`) and there is nothing to prove; assume n ≤ Q.

0. (Preliminaries on the chart.)
 (a) For w ∈ Ω and s ∈ ℝⁿ: w + ts ∈ Ω for small t, and |Φ(w+ts) − Φ(w)| ≥ c|t||s|; dividing by |t| and letting t → 0 gives |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|. So DΦ(w) is injective and T_w := DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w) has dimension n. Φ is injective on Ω; for y ∈ N let w_y ∈ Ω be the unique point with Φ(w_y) = y, and T_y := T_{w_y}. (The Lean conclusion “∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → …” concerns exactly w = w_y.)
 (b) Ψ := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ : N → Ω is (1/c)-Lipschitz. N is σ-compact (Ω is a countable union of compact sets and Φ is continuous), hence Borel; M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable.
 (c) N is locally Hⁿ-finite: if K ⊆ ℝ^Q is compact, Ψ(N ∩ K) has diameter ≤ diam(K)/c, so lies in a closed ball B̄ ⊆ ℝⁿ; Φ is Lipschitz on B̄ (C¹ on a compact convex set), say with constant Λ, and Hⁿ(N ∩ K) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞.
 (d) (Change of variables under blow-ups.) η_{y,λ} is a similarity of ratio λ⁻¹, so for every set S and every g ≥ 0 or Hⁿ⌞S-integrable g: ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n} ∫_S g∘η_{y,λ} dHⁿ (translation invariance and μHE[n](λS) = λⁿ μHE[n](S), Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`).
 (e) (C¹ blow-up of N; Simon: “since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim ∫_{η(N_j)} f = ∫_{T N_j} f”.) For every y ∈ N and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q): lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ. Proof: let spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), w := w_y. By (d) and the injective area formula for Φ on Ω (Φ injective, Lipschitz on bounded subsets of Ω; Simon Ch. 2 (3.2)/(3.5), SimonGMT `injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn` and its weighted fibre-sum form) the integral equals λ^{−n} ∫_Ω φ((Φ(v) − y)/λ) JΦ(v) dv, JΦ(v) := √det(DΦ(v)*DΦ(v)), and the substitution v = w + λs turns it into I_λ := ∫ 1_{(Ω−w)/λ}(s) φ((Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ) JΦ(w+λs) ds. If the integrand is nonzero then w, w + λs ∈ Ω and |Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w)| < λR, so c|λs| < λR, i.e. |s| < R/c. For λ ≤ 1 the integrand is bounded by sup|φ| · max_{|z−w| ≤ R/c} JΦ(z) and vanishes for |s| ≥ R/c; for fixed s, as λ ↓ 0: w + λs ∈ Ω eventually (Ω open), (Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ → DΦ(w)s and JΦ(w+λs) → JΦ(w). By dominated convergence I_λ → ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(DΦ(w)s) JΦ(w) ds = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ, the last equality being the linear area formula for the injective linear map DΦ(w) (Simon Ch. 2 (3.1); Mathlib `LinearMap.hausdorffMeasure_image`/normDet). Note that for nonnegative φ ≥ 1_{B_R(0)} this also shows sup_{0<λ≤1} λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) < ∞.
 (f) (Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT `Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6`.) If μ is a Borel regular measure on ℝ^Q and A is μ-measurable with μ(A) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ ℝ^Q ∖ A, lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} μ(A ∩ B_ρ(y)) = 0. (Finite Borel measures on ℝ^Q, and Hⁿ restricted to sets of finite measure, are Borel regular.)

1. (Compact pieces with continuous weight — Remark 1.8(1).) Let V_1 ⊆ V_2 ⊆ ⋯ be open sets with compact closures closure V_i ⊆ V_{i+1} ⊆ V and ⋃_i V_i = V. Fix i. ν_i(B) := ∫_{B ∩ M ∩ V_i} θ dHⁿ defines a finite Borel measure (∫_{M ∩ closure V_i} θ < ∞), and θ is ν_i-measurable (θ is a.e. strongly measurable on M ∩ closure V_i by `IntegrableOn`). Choose a Borel M_i′ ⊆ M ∩ V_i with Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ M_i′) = 0. For each j ≥ 1, Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure ν_i (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT `Chapter01.Lusin`) gives a closed F with ν_i(ℝ^Q ∖ F) < 1/(2j) and θ|F continuous, and inner regularity gives a compact C_{i,j} ⊆ M_i′ ∩ F with ν_i((M_i′ ∩ F) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/(2j). Thus C_{i,j} ⊆ M ∩ V_i is compact, θ|C_{i,j} is continuous and ν_i((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/j. Hence ν_i((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0, and since θ > 0 on M, also Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0. As M = ⋃_i (M ∩ V_i), it suffices to prove: for each fixed C := C_{i,j}, the conclusion holds at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N. Note that θ ≥ m_C := min_C θ > 0 on C (continuous positive function on a compact set), so Hⁿ(C) ≤ m_C^{−1} ∫_C θ dHⁿ < ∞.

2. (Unweighted tangent plane of C on the chart — proof of 1.6 “⇒”.) Exceptional sets, by (f):
 (i) μ := Hⁿ⌞C (finite), A := C ∖ N: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0.
 (ii) For each of the countably many rational balls B ⊆ ℝ^Q, μ := Hⁿ⌞(N ∩ B) (finite by (c)), A := (N ∩ B) ∖ C: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ B, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0; since B_ρ(y) ⊆ B for small ρ when y ∈ B, and the rational balls cover ℝ^Q: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0.
 Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy (i) and (ii). For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), using (d),
 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ = ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ − ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N ∖ C)} φ + ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C ∖ N)} φ,
 and |∫_{η_{y,λ}(N∖C)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, |∫_{η_{y,λ}(C∖N)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, while the first term tends to ∫_{T_y} φ by (e). Hence lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ (the exceptional set does not depend on φ). Moreover λ^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B_{λR}(y)) ≤ λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) + λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) stays bounded as λ ↓ 0 (by (e) and (i)).

3. (Exceptional set for the rest of M.) By (f) with μ := ν_i and A := (M ∩ V_i) ∖ C (ν_i(A) < ∞): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C, ρ^{−n} ∫_{((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C) ∩ B_ρ(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0.

4. (Weighted blow-up — Remark 1.8(1).) Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy the conclusions of steps 2 and 3, let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), and let λ > 0 be so small that closure B_{λR}(y) ⊆ V_i (possible: y ∈ C ⊆ V_i open). Then z ↦ φ(z)θ(y + λz) is Hⁿ-integrable on η_{y,λ}(M): it vanishes unless y + λz ∈ M ∩ B_{λR}(y), and by (d) its absolute integral is ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} ∫_{M ∩ closure B_{λR}(y)} θ < ∞. By (d),
 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y+λz) dHⁿ(z) = λ^{−n} ∫_M φ((x−y)/λ) θ(x) dHⁿ(x) = I₁ + I₂ + I₃, where
 I₁ := θ(y) λ^{−n} ∫_C φ((x−y)/λ) dHⁿ(x) = θ(y) ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ dHⁿ → θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ (step 2);
 I₂ := λ^{−n} ∫_{C ∩ B_{λR}(y)} φ((x−y)/λ)(θ(x) − θ(y)) dHⁿ(x), |I₂| ≤ sup|φ| · sup_{C ∩ B_{λR}(y)} |θ − θ(y)| · λ^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, because θ|C is continuous at y and the density ratio is bounded (step 2);
 I₃ := λ^{−n} ∫_{(M ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)} φ((x−y)/λ) θ(x) dHⁿ(x), and since (M ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y) = ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y), |I₃| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} ∫_{((M∩V_i)∖C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0 (step 3).
 Hence the weighted blow-up integrals converge to θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q); together with dim T_y = n (0(a)) this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T_y with T_y = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w_y).

5. (Conclusion.) The set of y ∈ M ∩ N where the conclusion fails is contained in ⋃_i ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) ∪ ⋃_{i,j} (the exceptional subsets of C_{i,j} ∩ N from steps 2–3), a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. Since M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable (0(b)), this is exactly the statement “∀ᵐ y ∂ Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)), ∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (range DΦ(w))”. ∎
 (For n = 0 all steps hold verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point, H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure, λ⁰ = 1, N is a single point or empty and T_y = {0}.)
proof_key_steps: Chart facts: DΦ(w) is injective with |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|; Φ(Ω) is σ-compact (hence Borel) and locally Hⁿ-finite; the inverse of Φ on Ω is (1/c)-Lipschitz.
C¹ blow-up: via the injective area formula and dominated convergence, blow-ups of Φ(Ω) at y = Φ(w) converge to Hⁿ⌞DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ).
Remark 1.8(1): by Lusin, M ∩ V_i is covered up to an Hⁿ-null set by compact C with θ|C continuous and Hⁿ(C) < ∞.
Proof of 1.6 '⇒': by the Upper Density Theorem, Hⁿ⌞(C∖N) and Hⁿ⌞(N∖C) have zero density at a.e. point of C ∩ N, so blow-ups of C converge to T_y with bounded density ratios.
The weighted blow-up of (M, θ) is θ(y)·(blow-up of C) + (continuity error on C) + (θHⁿ⌞(M∖C) term of zero density), giving the weighted tangent space T_y = range DΦ(w).

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); n := m + 1; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w; a map is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for w, w′ ∈ Ω. TG(f, G) is the tangential-gradient hypothesis of the statement. This is Step 7 of the parent proof (slicing_im_slice_triple), with its index pairs (j, k) merged into one index. The tangent identification fact used there is the sibling weighted_tangent_chart (slicing_im_st_weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart). The facts proved in steps 1, 2 and 6 below are, respectively, the content of the DAG nodes lpf_countably_rectifiable_c1_cover, lpf_c1_approximation_real and lpf_ccr_hasDerivAt_line_of_comp. Those may be used only after they are comparator-accepted and added as reuse children (byte-identical type and lean_name) at a decomposition of this node; the proof below is self-contained.
1. (C¹ charts for M; Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 'only if' and Remark 1.3, printed proof.) Claim: there are pairs (Φ′_i, Ω′_i), i ∈ ℕ, such that
   - Ω′_i ⊆ ℝⁿ is open;
   - Φ′_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is C¹, Lipschitz on Ω′_i and c′_i-antilipschitz on Ω′_i for some c′_i > 0;
   - Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i Φ′_i(Ω′_i)) = 0.
   Proof. By the field countablyRectifiable, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k F_k(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz (Simon 1.1). Fix k.
   (i) (C¹ approximation.) By Rademacher's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), F_k is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e. Apply the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5) to the P components with ε/P. For every l ≥ 1 this gives a C¹ map G_{kl} : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with Lⁿ({F_k ≠ G_{kl}} ∪ {DF_k ≠ DG_{kl}}) < 1/l, where the second set includes the points at which F_k is not differentiable. Put E_{kl} := {w : F_k is differentiable at w, F_k(w) = G_{kl}(w), DF_k(w) = DG_{kl}(w)} and Z_k := ℝⁿ ∖ ⋃_l E_{kl}. Then Lⁿ(Z_k) ≤ 1/l for every l, so Lⁿ(Z_k) = 0. Hence Hⁿ(F_k(Z_k)) ≤ Lip(F_k)ⁿ·Hⁿ(Z_k) = 0 (Lipschitz images; LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le rescaled to μHE[n], or SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).
   (ii) (Critical points.) Let C_{kl} := {w : DG_{kl}(w) is not injective}. Then Hⁿ(G_{kl}(C_{kl})) = 0, by the area formula for the locally Lipschitz map G_{kl} (Simon Ch. 2, §3): the Jacobian √det(DG_{kl}*DG_{kl}) vanishes on C_{kl}. In Lean, apply SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero on each ball B_R(0), R ∈ ℕ, to a Lipschitz extension (LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension) of G_{kl}|B_R(0). That extension has the same derivative as G_{kl} on the open ball.
   (iii) (Regular points.) Let w ∉ C_{kl}, A := DG_{kl}(w) (injective), μ_A := min_{|s|=1}|As| > 0 (μ_A := 1 if n = 0) and c := μ_A/2. By continuity of DG_{kl} choose r > 0 with ‖DG_{kl}(z) − A‖ ≤ c for |z − w| < r. The mean value inequality for z ↦ G_{kl}(z) − Az on the convex ball B_r(w) gives |G_{kl}(z) − G_{kl}(z′) − A(z − z′)| ≤ c|z − z′|. Hence |G_{kl}(z) − G_{kl}(z′)| ≥ 2c|z − z′| − c|z − z′| = c|z − z′| for z, z′ ∈ B_r(w). So G_{kl} is c-antilipschitz on every ball B with rational centre and rational radius such that w ∈ B and closure B ⊆ B_r(w). On such B, G_{kl} is also Lipschitz, because DG_{kl} is bounded on the compact convex set closure B (mean value inequality).
   (iv) Let (Φ′_i, Ω′_i)_{i∈ℕ} enumerate the countably many pairs (G_{kl}, B) such that k, l ∈ ℕ and B is a rational ball on which G_{kl} is Lipschitz and antilipschitz with a positive constant; pad with Ω′_i := ∅ if needed. Every w ∉ C_{kl} lies in such a ball (iii), and F_k = G_{kl} on E_{kl}. Hence F_k(ℝⁿ) ⊆ F_k(Z_k) ∪ ⋃_l G_{kl}(C_{kl}) ∪ ⋃_i Φ′_i(Ω′_i). Therefore M ∖ ⋃_i Φ′_i(Ω′_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k F_k(Z_k) ∪ ⋃_{k,l} G_{kl}(C_{kl}), a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. □
2. (C¹ approximation of f on the charts; Simon Ch. 2, 1.5.) Fix i.
   - Since f is L-Lipschitz and Φ′_i is Lipschitz on Ω′_i, u_i := f∘Φ′_i is Lipschitz on Ω′_i. Let ũ_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ be a Lipschitz extension of u_i|Ω′_i (McShane; LipschitzOnWith.extend_real).
   - By Rademacher's theorem ũ_i is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e. By the C¹ Approximation Theorem, for each k ≥ 1 there is a C¹ function h_{ik} : ℝⁿ → ℝ with Lⁿ({ũ_i ≠ h_{ik}} ∪ {Dũ_i ≠ Dh_{ik}}) < 1/k.
   - Put A′_{ik} := {w ∈ Ω′_i : ũ_i is differentiable at w, ũ_i(w) = h_{ik}(w), Dũ_i(w) = Dh_{ik}(w)}. Then Lⁿ(Ω′_i ∖ ⋃_k A′_{ik}) ≤ 1/k for every k, hence Lⁿ(Ω′_i ∖ ⋃_k A′_{ik}) = 0.
   - For w ∈ A′_{ik} ⊆ Ω′_i we have f(Φ′_i(w)) = u_i(w) = ũ_i(w) = h_{ik}(w). Since f∘Φ′_i = ũ_i on the open set Ω′_i ∋ w, f∘Φ′_i is differentiable at w with D(f∘Φ′_i)(w) = Dh_{ik}(w) (HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
3. (The data.) Enumerate (i, k) ∈ ℕ × ℕ by j ∈ ℕ (Nat.pair/Nat.unpair) and set Φ_j := Φ′_i, Ω_j := Ω′_i, A_j := A′_{ik}, h_j := h_{ik}. Then:
   - Ω_j is open; Φ_j is C¹ and c′_i-antilipschitz on Ω_j with c′_i > 0;
   - A_j ⊆ Ω_j and h_j is C¹;
   - f(Φ_j(w)) = h_j(w) for w ∈ A_j, and f∘Φ_j is differentiable at every w ∈ A_j with D(f∘Φ_j)(w) = Dh_j(w) (step 2).
4. (Coverage.) M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(A_j) ⊆ (M ∖ ⋃_i Φ′_i(Ω′_i)) ∪ ⋃_i Φ′_i(Ω′_i ∖ ⋃_k A′_{ik}).
   - The first set is Hⁿ-null by step 1.
   - Since Φ′_i is Lipschitz on Ω′_i, Hⁿ(Φ′_i(Ω′_i ∖ ⋃_k A′_{ik})) ≤ Lip(Φ′_i|Ω′_i)ⁿ·Lⁿ(Ω′_i ∖ ⋃_k A′_{ik}) = 0 (LipschitzOnWith Hausdorff image bound, Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ, step 2).
   Hence Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(A_j)) = 0.
5. (Tangent planes via the sibling.) For each j apply weighted_tangent_chart (slicing_im_st_weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart) with Q := P, dimension n, V := U, the set M, the weight θ, Φ := Φ_j and Ω := Ω_j. Its hypotheses hold:
   - U is open;
   - M ⊆ U is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U (fields subset, nullMeasurableSet, pos, integrableOn);
   - Ω_j is open, and Φ_j is C¹ and antilipschitz on Ω_j.
   It yields: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j) and all w ∈ Ω_j with Φ_j(w) = y, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (range DΦ_j(w)). This statement is vacuous for y ∉ Φ_j(Ω_j), so it holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.: split M into M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j) and M ∖ Φ_j(Ω_j) (ae_restrict_union_iff). Here Φ_j(Ω_j) is measurable as a continuous injective image of an open set (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; injectivity on Ω_j follows from the antilipschitz bound). By ae_all_iff, these countably many statements and TG(f, G) hold simultaneously at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M.
6. (Gradient identity.) Let x ∈ M be such a point, j ∈ ℕ and w ∈ A_j with Φ_j(w) = x, and put T := range DΦ_j(w).
   - By step 5, T is a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M, θ) at x. TG(f, G) with Q := T gives G(x) ∈ T and, for every v ∈ T, HasDerivAt (s ↦ f(x + sv)) ⟨G(x), v⟩ 0.
   - Fix u ∈ ℝⁿ and v := DΦ_j(w)u ∈ T. By directional derivatives (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10; parent Step 7), s ↦ f(x + sv) has derivative Dh_j(w)u at s = 0. Indeed f(x + sv) − f(x) = [f(Φ_j(w + su)) − f(Φ_j(w))] + [f(x + sv) − f(Φ_j(w + su))]. The first bracket is s·Dh_j(w)u + o(s), because f∘Φ_j is differentiable at w with derivative Dh_j(w) (step 3). The second has absolute value ≤ L·|Φ_j(w) + s·DΦ_j(w)u − Φ_j(w + su)| = o(s), because f is L-Lipschitz and Φ_j is differentiable at w.
   - By uniqueness of derivatives (HasDerivAt.unique), ⟨G(x), DΦ_j(w)u⟩ = Dh_j(w)u.
7. Steps 3–6 give every clause of the statement:
   - Ω_j is open, Φ_j is C¹ and antilipschitz on Ω_j, A_j ⊆ Ω_j, h_j is C¹, and f∘Φ_j = h_j on A_j;
   - Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(A_j)) = 0;
   - for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and all j, w ∈ A_j with Φ_j(w) = x: range DΦ_j(w) is a weighted approximate tangent plane at x, G(x) ∈ range DΦ_j(w), and ⟨G(x), DΦ_j(w)u⟩ = Dh_j(w)u for all u. ∎
proof_key_steps: Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2/Remark 1.3: C¹ approximation of the Lipschitz parametrizations, null critical images (area formula) and local antilipschitz estimates give countably many C¹ charts (Φ′_i, Ω′_i), Lipschitz and antilipschitz on Ω′_i, covering M up to an Hⁿ-null set.
C¹ approximation (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5) of a McShane extension of f∘Φ′_i: C¹ functions h_{ik} and sets A′_{ik} on which f∘Φ′_i = h_{ik} with equal derivatives; Lⁿ(Ω′_i ∖ ⋃_k A′_{ik}) = 0.
Merge the indices (i, k) into j; Lipschitz images of Lⁿ-null sets are Hⁿ-null, so Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(A_j)) = 0.
The sibling weighted_tangent_chart (dimension m+1) makes range DΦ_j(w) a weighted tangent plane of (M, θ) at Φ_j(w) a.e.
TG(f, G) plus directional derivatives (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10) give G(x) ∈ range DΦ_j(w) and ⟨G(x), DΦ_j(w)u⟩ = Dh_j(w)u.

subproblems.title: Regular level sets on a C¹ antilipschitz chart are covered by countably many C¹ bi-Lipschitz m-charts
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^P of class C¹, Ω ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} open with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω (some c > 0), h : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ of class C¹ and t ∈ ℝ. Then there are C¹ maps Ψ_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and open sets V_i ⊆ ℝ^m (i ∈ ℕ) such that each Ψ_i is Lipschitz on V_i and c_i-antilipschitz on V_i for some c_i > 0; for every w ∈ Ω with h(w) = t and Dh(w) ≠ 0 there are i and v ∈ V_i with Ψ_i(v) = Φ(w); and for every i and v ∈ V_i there is w ∈ Ω with h(w) = t, Ψ_i(v) = Φ(w) and DΨ_i(v)(ℝ^m) = DΦ(w)(ker Dh(w)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (h : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ) (t : ℝ), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ContDiff ℝ 1 h → ∃ (Ψ : ℕ → Eucl m → Eucl P) (V : ℕ → Set (Eucl m)), (∀ i, IsOpen (V i)) ∧ (∀ i, ContDiff ℝ 1 (Ψ i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K (Ψ i) (V i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ V i, ∀ v' ∈ V i, c * ‖v - v'‖ ≤ ‖Ψ i v - Ψ i v'‖) ∧ (∀ w ∈ Ω, h w = t → fderiv ℝ h w ≠ 0 → ∃ i, ∃ v ∈ V i, Ψ i v = Φ w) ∧ ∀ i, ∀ v ∈ V i, ∃ w ∈ Ω, h w = t ∧ Ψ i v = Φ w ∧ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (Ψ i) v).toLinearMap = Submodule.map (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap (LinearMap.ker (fderiv ℝ h w).toLinearMap)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. B(v, r) is the open ball. Dψ(v) := fderiv ℝ ψ v. A map is c-antilipschitz on a set if c|v − v′| ≤ |ψ(v) − ψ(v′)| there. This is the implicit-function part of Step 8 of the parent proof (slicing_im_slice_triple): 'by the implicit function theorem the set {w ∈ Ω_j : h_{jk}(w) = t, ∇h_{jk}(w) ≠ 0} is covered by countably many C¹ parametrizations ψ : V → ℝⁿ (V ⊆ ℝ^m open, Dψ injective, ψ bi-Lipschitz on V after shrinking), and Ψ := Φ_j∘ψ is C¹, Lipschitz on V with a positive lower Lipschitz bound'. Here it is made precise.
0. (Trivial case.) Let R := {w ∈ Ω : h(w) = t, Dh(w) ≠ 0}. If R = ∅, take V_i := ∅ and Ψ_i :≡ 0 for all i: every clause holds (vacuously, the antilipschitz clause with c_i := 1). Assume R ≠ ∅.
1. (Local graph parametrization at w₀ ∈ R.) Fix w₀ ∈ R and let ℓ := Dh(w₀) ≠ 0. Let a ∈ ℝ^{m+1} be its gradient (ℓ(u) = ⟨a, u⟩, a ≠ 0) and e := a/|a|², so ℓ(e) = 1. The kernel K₀ := ker ℓ = a^⊥ has dimension m. Fix a linear isometry ι₀ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} with range K₀ (from an orthonormal basis of K₀ indexed by Fin m; ι₀ = 0 if m = 0). Define the C¹ function H : ℝ^m × ℝ → ℝ, H(v, s) := h(w₀ + ι₀v + se). Then H(0, 0) = t, and the partial derivative of H in s at (0, 0) is s ↦ s·ℓ(e) = s, which is invertible. By the implicit function theorem (Mathlib ContDiffAt.implicitFunction with implicitFunction_apply_self, eventually_apply_eq_iff_implicitFunction and contDiffAt_implicitFunction) there are a function g : ℝ^m → ℝ with g(0) = 0 that is C¹ at 0, and a neighbourhood N₀ of (0, 0) such that for (v, s) ∈ N₀: H(v, s) = t ⟺ s = g(v). Since g is C¹ at 0 it is C¹ on a neighbourhood of 0 (ContDiffAt.eventually); choose r₀ > 0 such that g is C¹ on B(0, 3r₀).
2. (Globalization.) Let χ : ℝ^m → [0, 1] be a C^∞ bump function with χ = 1 on B(0, r₀) and support in B(0, 2r₀) (ContDiffBump). Put g̃ := χ·g. Then g̃ is C¹ on ℝ^m: it is C¹ on B(0, 3r₀) as a product of C¹ functions, and it vanishes identically on the open set {|v| > 2r₀}; these two open sets cover ℝ^m. Moreover g̃ = g on B(0, r₀). Put ψ(v) := w₀ + ι₀v + g̃(v)e. Then ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m+1} is C¹ and ψ(0) = w₀.
3. (ψ is 1-antilipschitz on ℝ^m.) ψ(v) − ψ(v′) = ι₀(v − v′) + (g̃(v) − g̃(v′))e with ι₀(v − v′) ∈ a^⊥ ⟂ e. By Pythagoras |ψ(v) − ψ(v′)|² = |v − v′|² + (g̃(v) − g̃(v′))²|e|² ≥ |v − v′|². Consequently Dψ(v) is injective with |Dψ(v)u| ≥ |u|, because |Dψ(v)u| = lim_{s→0} |ψ(v + su) − ψ(v)|/|s|.
4. (Chart domain.) Let A₀(v, s) := w₀ + ι₀v + se. Its linear part (v, s) ↦ ι₀v + se is a linear isomorphism ℝ^m × ℝ → ℝ^{m+1}: it is injective because ι₀ is injective with range a^⊥ and e ∉ a^⊥, and the dimensions agree. Hence A₀ is a homeomorphism. Choose r₁ > 0 and δ > 0 with B(0, r₁) × (−δ, δ) ⊆ N₀. Then choose r ∈ (0, min(r₀, r₁)] so small that for |v| < r: |g(v)| < δ (g is continuous at 0 and g(0) = 0); ψ(v) ∈ Ω (ψ is continuous, ψ(0) = w₀ ∈ Ω, Ω open); and Dh(ψ(v)) ≠ 0 (Dh is continuous and Dh(w₀) ≠ 0). Put V := B(0, r) and W := A₀(B(0, r) × (−δ, δ)), an open neighbourhood of w₀.
5. (The level set inside W is ψ(V).)
   - Let w ∈ W with h(w) = t. Write w = A₀(v, s) with |v| < r and |s| < δ. Then (v, s) ∈ N₀ and H(v, s) = h(w) = t, so s = g(v) = g̃(v) (as |v| < r ≤ r₀). Hence w = ψ(v) with v ∈ V.
   - Conversely, for v ∈ V we have (v, g(v)) ∈ B(0, r) × (−δ, δ) ⊆ N₀, so H(v, g(v)) = t. As ψ(v) = A₀(v, g(v)), this says h(ψ(v)) = t.
6. (The chart Ψ := Φ∘ψ on V.)
   - Ψ is C¹ as a composition of C¹ maps.
   - Ψ is Lipschitz on V: DΨ is continuous, hence bounded by some K on the compact convex set closedBall(0, r), so Ψ is K-Lipschitz on V by the mean value inequality (Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le).
   - Ψ is c-antilipschitz on V: for v, v′ ∈ V, ψ(v), ψ(v′) ∈ Ω (step 4), so |Ψ(v) − Ψ(v′)| ≥ c|ψ(v) − ψ(v′)| ≥ c|v − v′| (step 3).
7. (Tangent spaces.) Let v ∈ V and w := ψ(v); then w ∈ Ω and h(w) = t (steps 4, 5), and Ψ(v) = Φ(w).
   - Since h∘ψ ≡ t on the open set V ∋ v, D(h∘ψ)(v) = Dh(w)∘Dψ(v) = 0, so range Dψ(v) ⊆ ker Dh(w).
   - range Dψ(v) has dimension m (step 3), and ker Dh(w) has dimension m since Dh(w) ≠ 0 (step 4). Hence range Dψ(v) = ker Dh(w).
   - By the chain rule DΨ(v) = DΦ(w)∘Dψ(v), so range DΨ(v) = DΦ(w)(range Dψ(v)) = DΦ(w)(ker Dh(w)).
8. (Countably many charts.) Steps 1–7 give, for each w₀ ∈ R, a triple (Ψ_{w₀}, V_{w₀}, W_{w₀}) with W_{w₀} an open neighbourhood of w₀. Every w ∈ W_{w₀} with h(w) = t is ψ_{w₀}(v) for some v ∈ V_{w₀}, so Φ(w) = Ψ_{w₀}(v). Since ℝ^{m+1} is second countable, the family {W_{w₀} : w₀ ∈ R} has a countable subfamily with the same union (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). That union contains R. Enumerate the countable subfamily, nonempty since R ≠ ∅, as w_i (i ∈ ℕ, repetitions allowed), and set Ψ_i := Ψ_{w_i}, V_i := V_{w_i}.
9. (Verification.)
   - Each V_i is open; each Ψ_i is C¹, Lipschitz on V_i and c-antilipschitz on V_i (step 6).
   - If w ∈ Ω, h(w) = t and Dh(w) ≠ 0, then w ∈ R lies in some W_{w_i}, so Φ(w) = Ψ_i(v) for some v ∈ V_i (step 8).
   - For v ∈ V_i, w := ψ_{w_i}(v) satisfies w ∈ Ω, h(w) = t, Ψ_i(v) = Φ(w) and range DΨ_i(v) = DΦ(w)(ker Dh(w)) (step 7).
   For m = 0 every step holds verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point, ι₀ = 0, V = ℝ⁰, ψ ≡ w₀ and Ψ ≡ Φ(w₀). Then range DΨ = {0} = DΦ(w₀)(ker Dh(w₀)), because Dh(w₀) ≠ 0 is injective on ℝ¹, and the regular points of the level set are isolated. ∎
proof_key_steps: At a regular point w₀ of the level set {h = t} ∩ Ω, the implicit function theorem for H(v, s) = h(w₀ + ι₀v + se), with ι₀ an isometry onto ker Dh(w₀) and Dh(w₀)e = 1, gives a C¹ graph function g.
Globalize g with a bump function. ψ(v) = w₀ + ι₀v + g̃(v)e is C¹ on ℝ^m and 1-antilipschitz by Pythagoras.
Shrink to a ball V so that ψ(V) ⊆ Ω, Dh ≠ 0 on ψ(V), and the level set inside an open W ∋ w₀ is exactly ψ(V).
Ψ := Φ∘ψ is C¹, Lipschitz on V (mean value inequality) and c-antilipschitz on V, with range DΨ(v) = DΦ(ψ v)(ker Dh(ψ v)) by dimension count.
A countable subcover of the open sets W (second countability) gives the charts Ψ_i, V_i.

subproblems.title: Almost every slice M_t is countably m-rectifiable with weighted tangent plane T_xM ∩ G(x)^⊥ (Simon Ch. 6, 4.1)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m+1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, (M, θ, ξ) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz, and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel with |G(x)| ≤ L for all x and the tangential-gradient property (for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every weighted approximate tangent plane Q of (M, θ) at x: G(x) ∈ Q and d/ds f(x + su)|_{s=0} = ⟨G(x), u⟩ for u ∈ Q). Assume the co-area identity for (M, f, G): for every Borel g ≥ 0, t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_M |G| g dHⁿ (Hᵏ := μHE[k]). Let M_t := {x ∈ M : f(x) = t, G(x) ≠ 0}. Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ: M_t is countably m-rectifiable; and for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_t and every weighted approximate tangent plane Q of (M, θ) at x, the subspace Q ∩ G(x)^⊥ = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙G(x))ᗮ is a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M_t, θ) at x (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M_t θ x).

   - for every v ∈ V_{j,i} there is w′ ∈ Ω_j with h_j(w′) = t, Ψ_{j,i}(v) = Φ_j(w′) and range DΨ_{j,i}(v) = DΦ_j(w′)(ker Dh_j(w′)).

   Proof. By p(x), x = Φ_j(w) for some j and w ∈ A_j. With T := range DΦ_j(w): T is a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M, θ) at x, G(x) ∈ T, and ⟨G(x), DΦ_j(w)u⟩ = Dh_j(w)u for all u.
   (a) h_j(w) = f(Φ_j(w)) = f(x) = t.
   (b) Dh_j(w) ≠ 0: write G(x) = DΦ_j(w)u₀; then Dh_j(w)u₀ = ⟨G(x), G(x)⟩ = |G(x)|², which is nonzero because G(x) ≠ 0 (x ∈ M_t).

Ψ_{j,i}(V_{j,i}) is measurable by Lusin–Souslin (Ψ_{j,i} is continuous and injective on the open set V_{j,i}; MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), and the statement is vacuous off Ψ_{j,i}(V_{j,i}). Step 4 gives (j, i, v) with Ψ_{j,i}(v) = x and range DΨ_{j,i}(v) = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙G(x))ᗮ, and step 6 says that range DΨ_{j,i}(v) is a weighted approximate tangent plane of (M_t, θ) at x. So HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M_t θ x (Q ⊓ (ℝ∙G(x))ᗮ). With step 5, both conclusions hold for every t in a set of full L¹-measure. ∎

subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, τ : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^P orthonormal, g ∈ span(range τ) with g ≠ 0, and w an (m+1)-vector with w = simpleNVector τ or w = −simpleNVector τ. Put ν := |g|⁻¹g and let w⌞ν := w ∘ ι(ν) be the m-vector α ↦ w(ν♭∧α), where ι(ν) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ ℝ^P ℝ) ∘ (smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m (innerSL ℝ ν)), i.e. (ν♭∧α)(v₀,…,v_m) = Σ_i (−1)^i ⟨ν, v_i⟩ α(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_m). Then there is an orthonormal τ′ : Fin m → ℝ^P with span(range τ′) = span(range τ) ∩ g^⊥ (= span(range τ) ⊓ (ℝ∙g)ᗮ) and w⌞ν = simpleNVector τ′ or w⌞ν = −simpleNVector τ′.

Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. Λ^k := Covector (Eucl P) k is the space of continuous alternating k-forms, and a k-vector is a continuous linear functional on Λ^k. simpleNVector σ is the k-vector α ↦ α(σ) (simpleNVector_apply). For v ∈ ℝ^P, ι(v) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ ℝ^P ℝ) ∘L (smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m (innerSL ℝ v)). By `rfl`, ι(v)α = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α), and by alternatizeUncurryFin_apply, (ι(v)α)(σ) = Σ_{i : Fin (m+1)} (−1)^i ⟨v, σ_i⟩ α(removeNth i σ). This is Step 10 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 4.3); the frame-sign fact (Fact F of the parent) is the sibling frame_sign (fiw_ims_frame_sign).
1. (The subspace S.) Let T := span(range τ). Since τ is orthonormal it is linearly independent, so dim T = m + 1. Since g ∈ T and g ≠ 0, ν := |g|⁻¹g is a unit vector in T. Let S := T ⊓ (ℝ∙g)ᗮ = {v ∈ T : ⟨g, v⟩ = 0} (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right). The linear functional v ↦ ⟨g, v⟩ on T is nonzero, since ⟨g, g⟩ = |g|² ≠ 0, and S is its kernel. By rank–nullity, dim S = m.
2. (Orthonormal basis τ′ of S.) Choose an orthonormal basis of S indexed by Fin m (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ S reindexed along dim S = m), and let τ′_i ∈ ℝ^P be its vectors. The inner product of S is the restriction of that of ℝ^P, so τ′ : Fin m → ℝ^P is orthonormal, and span(range τ′) = S. This gives the first two conclusions.
3. (Adapted frame.) Let σ := Fin.snoc τ′ ν : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^P, i.e. σ = (τ′_0, …, τ′_{m−1}, ν). σ is orthonormal: τ′ is orthonormal, |ν| = 1, and ⟨τ′_i, ν⟩ = |g|⁻¹⟨τ′_i, g⟩ = 0 since τ′_i ∈ S. The m + 1 vectors of σ lie in T (S ⊆ T, ν ∈ T) and are linearly independent, and dim T = m + 1, so span(range σ) = T = span(range τ).
4. (Frame sign.) By frame_sign (fiw_ims_frame_sign) applied to τ and σ, simpleNVector σ = simpleNVector τ or simpleNVector σ = −simpleNVector τ. Together with w = ±simpleNVector τ, this gives w = ε·simpleNVector σ for some ε ∈ {1, −1}.
5. (Evaluation.) Let α ∈ Λ^m. In (ι(ν)α)(σ) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ α(removeNth i σ):
   - for i = castSucc k (k < m), σ_i = τ′_k and ⟨ν, τ′_k⟩ = 0;
   - for i = last m, σ_i = ν, ⟨ν, ν⟩ = 1, and removeNth (last m) σ = init σ = τ′ (Fin.removeNth_last, Fin.init_snoc).
   Splitting the sum with Fin.sum_univ_castSucc gives (ι(ν)α)(σ) = (−1)^m α(τ′).
6. (Conclusion.) For every α ∈ Λ^m, (w ∘L ι(ν))(α) = ε·simpleNVector σ (ι(ν)α) = ε·(ι(ν)α)(σ) = ε(−1)^m α(τ′) = ε(−1)^m·simpleNVector τ′ (α). By extensionality of continuous linear maps, w ∘L ι(ν) = ε(−1)^m·simpleNVector τ′ with ε(−1)^m ∈ {1, −1}, so w ∘L ι(ν) is simpleNVector τ′ or −simpleNVector τ′.
   For m = 0, τ′ is the empty family, S = {0}, σ = (ν), simpleNVector τ′ is evaluation at the empty tuple, and the same computation applies. ∎
proof_key_steps: S := span τ ∩ g^⊥ is the kernel of the nonzero functional ⟨g, ·⟩ on the (m+1)-dimensional span τ, so dim S = m; take an orthonormal basis τ′ of S indexed by Fin m.
σ := (τ′, ν) with ν = g/|g| is an orthonormal basis of span τ, so frame_sign gives w = ±simpleNVector σ.
alternatizeUncurryFin_apply: (ν♭∧α)(σ) = (−1)^m α(τ′), since ⟨ν, τ′_k⟩ = 0, ⟨ν, ν⟩ = 1 and removeNth (last m) σ = τ′.
By extensionality, w ∘ ι(ν) = ±simpleNVector τ′.

subproblems.title: Orthonormal frames of the same subspace have the same simple n-vector up to sign
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P be orthonormal families with span(range τ) = span(range τ'). Then simpleNVector τ' = simpleNVector τ or simpleNVector τ' = −simpleNVector τ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ τ' : Fin n → Eucl P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Orthonormal ℝ τ' → Submodule.span ℝ (range τ) = Submodule.span ℝ (range τ') → simpleNVector τ' = simpleNVector τ ∨ simpleNVector τ' = -simpleNVector τ

Provenance: this child reuses the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.fiw_ims_frame_sign of DAG node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.frame_sign-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit c90a40505abdbff33b9174acf9b20037eb2cb2a1, no dependencies). Its frozen Lean type, title and statement are copied byte-for-byte from that node. The proof below is that node's accepted proof, copied verbatim; it is self-contained. Use in slicing_im_slice_triple: Fact F (frame sign) of the parent proof, Step 10, consumed through the new child interior_product (slicing_im_st_interior_product), step 4.

1. (Two orthonormal bases of Q.) Let Q := span(range τ) = span(range τ').
   - An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of Q (Basis.span).
   - It is orthonormal for the inner product of Q, which is the ambient one. Call this orthonormal basis b of Q (Basis.toOrthonormalBasis).
   - In the same way τ' is an orthonormal basis of span(range τ') = Q. Transporting along this equality of submodules gives an orthonormal basis b' of Q with b'_j = τ'_j.
   - In particular dim Q = n.

2. (Change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector on ℝ^P.
   - Its restriction f := α ∘ (inclusion Q ↪ ℝ^P), f(v_1, …, v_n) := α(v_1, …, v_n), is an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q (AlternatingMap.compLinearMap with Q.subtype).
   - By AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, f = f(b)·b.det.
   - Evaluating at b': α(τ') = f(b') = f(b)·b.det(b') = d·α(τ), where d := b.det(b') does not depend on α.
   - Elementary version: τ'_j = Σ_i O_{ij} τ_i with O_{ij} = ⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩, because τ'_j ∈ Q and τ is an orthonormal basis of Q. Multilinearity and alternation give α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ), and d = det O.

3. (d = ±1.) b.det(b') is the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix between the orthonormal bases b and b' of Q. That matrix is orthogonal, so d = 1 or d = −1 (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Elementary version: OᵀO = I because τ' is orthonormal, so d² = 1.

4. (Conclusion.)
   - For every α: (simpleNVector τ')(α) = α(τ') = d·α(τ) = (d • simpleNVector τ)(α) (simpleNVector_apply).
   - By extensionality of continuous linear maps, simpleNVector τ' = d • simpleNVector τ. This is simpleNVector τ if d = 1 and −simpleNVector τ if d = −1.
   - For n = 0 both families are empty, Q = 0, d = 1, and both sides are evaluation at the empty tuple. ∎
proof_key_steps: τ and τ' are orthonormal bases of the same n-dimensional subspace Q
restrict α to Q: α(τ') = b.det(b')·α(τ) by AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det
b.det(b') = ±1 since the change of basis between orthonormal bases is orthogonal
extensionality: simpleNVector τ' = ±simpleNVector τ
